text:
remy: quick heads-up onboarding Cust-Argo LoRA 'NumFuse' into staging. ran merge+quant smoke and seeing systematic magnitude blow-ups on invoice totals. tiny thread.
remy: example mismatch:
```
pred: "Invoice total: $10,000"
truth: "Invoice total: $100.00"
conf: 0.93
```
zoe: :grimacing: different from the usual token-id issue. which quant path did you test? GPTQ/GGUF/AWQ/QLoRA variants?
remy: tested three quick paths: A) GPTQ blockwise int4 (our old default) B) AWQ per-channel int4 (newer) C) QLoRA-style 4-bit nF4 fuse + LoRA reapply. Merge was standard merge alpha=0.5 adapter.
jun: interesting. could be per-layer scale underflow in GPTQ producing exaggerated logits for digit tokens. also check fused bias handling during LoRA apply.
remy: kicking quickpacks:
- cb-arg-001: GPTQ-int4 + merged (seed 2)
- cb-arg-002: AWQ-int4 per-channel + merged
- cb-arg-003: QLoRA-nf4 reserialize + merged
ci-bot: CI started: cb-arg-001, cb-arg-002, cb-arg-003 (jobs remy).
remy: also ran a float16 baseline for reference.
ci-bot: cb-arg-001 (GPTQ-int4) done: overall acc 0.76 (baseline float16 0.80) numeric F1 0.49 vs baseline 0.67, many x100/x10 magnitude errors.
ci-bot: cb-arg-002 (AWQ-int4) done: overall acc 0.78, numeric F1 0.60, magnitude error ~1.4x median.
ci-bot: cb-arg-003 (QLoRA-nf4 reserialize) done: overall acc 0.80, numeric F1 0.66, magnitude error ~1.05x (closest to baseline).
paul: wow GPTQ-int4 regressed the most. that matches a hypothesis: blockwise scale quant can collapse small activation ranges used for digit tokens and amplify rare-token logits.
zoe: do we have per-layer activation scale diffs? a quick plot of layerwise scale before/after quant would help. also check whether LoRA apply fused bias got quantized away in GPTQ path.
jun: run `diag/scale_scan.py --model numfuse --quant-path GPTQ` and dump top-3 layers with largest scale shifts.
remy: ran diag: GPTQ top scale-shift layers: 7, 11, 22 (up to 12x shift). AWQ had max 2.3x shift. QLoRA-nf4 under 1.2x.
paul: okay that explains the numeric blow-ups for GPTQ. low-level advice: prefer AWQ or nF4 for customer adapters with numeric-heavy prompts, or add per-layer bias correction after quant.
marta: action items for onboarding docs / CI:
- add a "quant bakeoff" matrix for adapters: run GPTQ/AWQ/QLoRA-nf4 and score numeric-heavy evalsets automatically
- if GPTQ is significantly worse, default to AWQ/nF4 for that adapter and flag in console
- add a quick diag step to surface top layer scale-shifts and recommend hybrid mixing (int8 for layers with >4x shift)
remy: ran a hybrid experiment: keep layers 0-6 int8 under GPTQ path, rest GPTQ-int4 -> cb-arg-004.
ci-bot: cb-arg-004 (GPTQ-hybrid int8 prefix) done: numeric F1 0.62, magnitude error 1.2x. improved but still behind AWQ/nF4.
zoe: ok viable but more operational complexity. probably better to prefer AWQ/nF4 by default and use hybrid only if customer insists on GPTQ artifacts.
jun: small note: also test with LoRA merge alpha variations (0.7/0.3 base/adapter) - heavier base tends to damp new-token spikes.
remy: did a quick alpha sweep (0.6/0.4, 0.8/0.2) under QLoRA-nf4, results: 0.8/0.2 + nF4 gave slight quality boost and fewer outliers.
paul: propose rollout plan for customer:
- immediate: use QLoRA-nF4 reserialize + merge 0.8/0.2 as canary for invoices pipeline
- infra: add quant-bakeoff CI step that runs AWQ and nF4 and stores per-layer scale diagnostics
- fallback: float16 shadow if any canary regression above threshold
marta: I'll add the bakeoff to adapter onboarding template and update console recommendations. also adding a one-pager on quant-path tradeoffs for customer success.
remy: thanks all. I'll write the EOD note to customer recommending nF4 route and attach the quickpack artifacts. tagging @ops-bot to schedule a canary.
ops-bot: scheduled canary: numfuse-nf4-canary starting 2023-07-24T20:00Z (approx).
remy: closing loop, will post if the canary surfaces anything.
